title: 2025 budget public input session
subtitle: Downtown Ambassador program funding, accessible Challenger Baseball diamond, and extra community events money drew delegate comment.
overview: The Finance and Corporate Services Committee held a public input session on the proposed 2025 budget. No motions were recorded other than adjourning, so the committee made no recommendations. The meeting was for listening to residents, and any changes to the budget would come later.

Staff outlined the budget and its schedule. The Mayor is to formally propose the budget on December 2, 2024, and Final Budget Day is December 12, 2024. Staff said the proposed tax rate increase is 3.9%, and that Kitchener's total municipal burden is below the average for large Ontario municipalities.

Three delegates spoke. The Kitchener Downtown BIA supported continuing the Downtown Ambassador program run by By-law Enforcement, and councillors asked whether the BIA could help fund it. Kitchener Minor Baseball backed an accessible Challenger Baseball diamond at Upper Canada Park. The Caribana Ignite Festival supported the proposed additional $200,000 for community events. Residents with questions can contact staff before Final Budget Day.
debate: The BIA delegate said the ambassador program helps vulnerable people and reduces unnecessary 911 calls, which supports downtown businesses and visitors.

Several councillors asked whether the BIA could share the cost of the Downtown Ambassador program instead of leaving it to taxpayers, noting the BIA previously funded it. The delegate said the BIA's 2025 budget is already approved, a board vote would be needed, and the request could be raised with the board.

The BIA delegate said the BIA could not run the program itself, since it was less effective as needs grew more complex. The BIA board also decided that social issues are not typically a BIA responsibility. The delegate noted downtown serves residents of every ward.

The Challenger Baseball delegate said the current field lacks accessibility features. An accessible diamond at Upper Canada Park would serve children with disabilities, and the nearest accessible diamond for tournaments is in Scarborough.
The Caribana Ignite delegate said the extra community events funding would support diverse festivals, local vendors and visitors. The delegate said an economic impact study is still pending.
